request.prompt:
Image 1 is a motor-axis layout guide only. Replace dots and lines with a complete industrial product and omit all visible guide marks.
Design a quadcopter for everyday carry-along aerial photography. Strict orthographic top view, nose toward the top edge of the image, arms fully unfolded.
Four motors in a True X layout: the four motor centres sit at the corners of a square. Mean opposite-motor (diagonal) span 250 mm; motor-centre width-to-length span ratio W/L 1.00; adjacent arm angles clockwise from the front-left motor: 90°, 90°, 90°, 90°.
Match the motor centres and frame links in the attached layout image: dots mark motor centres, lines mark frame links. Do not reproduce the dots or lines in the result.
Each motor carries one stationary 2-blade propeller, 5-inch (127 mm) diameter. The two blades point in exactly opposite directions from the hub.
No propeller guards.
Each arm is 15 mm wide and 4 mm thick; seen from above it reads as a 15 mm wide beam.
Fuselage design envelope 150 × 55 × 30 mm (length × width × height); this is a size limit, not a shape.
A forward-facing camera sits at the nose and looks horizontally toward the top edge of the image; no lens glass faces the viewer, and nothing camera-like appears at the tail.
Low landing skids with 40 mm ground clearance, tucked beneath the aircraft.
Show the complete product on a plain light background as a photorealistic industrial design rendering. Omit guide marks, dimensions and lettering.
Image 2 is the appearance parent to revise. Preserve its visual identity while applying the current layout and design changes.
Design goal for this version: 只改机鼻：让前向相机与机鼻衔接更协调；四处机臂与机身的连接保持不变。
request.negative_prompt: flat schematic, line drawing, collage, text, labels, logo, cropped rotor, disconnected arm, extra rotor, perspective camera, V-shaped propeller, blades at an acute angle, single-blade propeller, missing blade, unequal blades
